new_scholarship.name: International Student Merit Scholarship
new_scholarship.duration: For the entire duration of the course; the reduction is applied at the commencement of each session for as long as the recipient remains enrolled and meets the conditions. CSU publishes no fixed number of years, because it depends on the degree programme.
new_scholarship.deadline: Applications open; Closes: 11:59pm 31 Dec 2026. The How to Apply section separately states 'Applications are open until further advice.'
new_scholarship.application_period: Rolling: applications are open and assessed as part of the course admissions process, with the award page stating a closing date of 11:59pm 31 Dec 2026 and also that applications are open until further advice. CSU does not publish intake-by-intake scholarship windows for this award.
new_scholarship.application_method: Automatic on admission. There is no separate scholarship application: 'Your application for this scholarship will be automatically considered by our admissions team when you apply for an eligible course on an eligible campus' and 'There is no additional application process.' The outcome is advised with the offer letter, and the award appears on the offer letter.
new_scholarship.description: The International Student Merit Scholarship is a Charles Sturt University tuition-fee reduction for new commencing international students. It provides a 25% fee discount for the entire duration of the course, deducted from tuition fees at the commencement of each session. It is awarded automatically by the admissions team when an applicant applies for an eligible course in internal/on-campus mode at an eligible campus; there is no separate application form and the outcome is advised with the offer letter. Academic entry is assessed either through an Australian AQF Level 7 route or through published Year 12 equivalent percentage thresholds of 75% for most undergraduate degrees and 85% for Allied Health courses other than Nursing.
new_scholarship.best_fit: New international applicants to Charles Sturt University who are commencing an approved on-campus undergraduate degree at an eligible regional or metropolitan campus and who can meet a published Year 12 equivalent academic entry score. Not suitable for continuing students, transfer students from another CSU course, online-mode starters, international exchange or study abroad students, or students already holding an Australia Awards or Research Training Program scholarship.
new_scholarship.funding_period: per academic session, for the duration of the course
new_scholarship.eligibility_summary: Open to new commencing international applicants studying an approved course in internal/on-campus mode at the Albury-Wodonga, Bathurst, Dubbo, Melbourne, Orange, Port Macquarie, Sydney or Wagga Wagga campuses. Not available to continuing or transferring students, international exchange or study abroad applicants, students commencing an online-mode course, students commencing at a CSU international partner, or students holding an Australia Awards or Research Training Program scholarship. Applicants must satisfy one of two published academic routes: an Australian academic progression route (AQF Level 7 or above completed in Australia within 12 months of course commencement) or a general academic route requiring 85 per cent in equivalent Australian Year 12 for an eligible Allied Health course other than Nursing, 75 per cent for any other eligible undergraduate degree, or 65 per cent for an eligible postgraduate degree. The scholarship is assessed as part of the admissions process and cannot be held together with another Charles Sturt-funded tuition fee scholarship.
eligibility: Be a new commencing international applicant for an approved course offered by Charles Sturt University.
Study in internal/on-campus mode at an eligible campus (Albury-Wodonga, Bathurst, Dubbo, Melbourne, Orange, Port Macquarie, Sydney or Wagga Wagga).
Not be a continuing or transferring student, and not transfer from another Charles Sturt course.
Not be an International Exchange or Study Abroad applicant.
Not be commencing an online-mode course or a course at a Charles Sturt international partner.
Not already hold an Australia Awards or Research Training Program (RTP) scholarship.
Satisfy one of the two published academic criteria: the Australian academic progression route, or the general academic entry-score route.

Australian academic progression route: have completed an Australian AQF Level 7 or higher qualification in Australia, offshore or online, with the completion date within 12 months of the applied course commencement date, and be new to CSU or new to that level of study.

General academic route: academic entry score of 85 per cent in equivalent Australian Year 12 for an eligible Allied Health course except Nursing, 75 per cent for any other eligible undergraduate degree, or 65 per cent in equivalent Australian undergraduate study for an eligible postgraduate degree.
Enrol in a course from the published list of approved undergraduate or postgraduate courses with the matching entry-score threshold.
Meet the Genuine Student requirement, including financial capacity, and pay the appropriate fee deposit to receive a Confirmation of Enrolment (e-COE).
coverage: A 25% reduction in tuition fees, applied for the entire duration of the course and deducted from tuition fees at the commencement of each session while the conditions are met.
benefits: 25% tuition fee reduction for the duration of the course.
Automatic consideration: no separate scholarship application is required.
Award confirmed in the offer letter issued with the admission offer.
May be deferred to a future intake and still be awarded.
May be transferred to another campus provided the student remains in the same course and meets the criteria.
An Approved Leave of Absence does not terminate the scholarship.
requirements: Apply for admission to an approved Charles Sturt University course in internal/on-campus mode at an eligible campus; this single application is also the scholarship application.

Accept the offer of study at the university and make the appropriate fee deposit to receive a e-COE.

Maintain satisfactory academic progress and continued enrolment to keep the scholarship active.

Sign a media release authorising the use of your photographs and images for promotional and marketing purposes, and agree to provide information, testimonials and promotional content.

Evidence of the academic entry score for the approved course, assessed by CSU against the published Year 12 equivalent thresholds.

Fee deposit receipt and e-COE, as part of accepting the offer.
Signed media release, provided by the University after award.
new_scholarship.selection_notes: There is no separate selection committee and no published scoring weighting: 'Applicants will be considered as part of their course admissions process.' CSU states it will 'award as many scholarships as possible, with an intent to reward every eligible student', so the academic entry threshold is the operative filter rather than a ranked competition. The scholarship outcome is advised with the offer letter.
new_scholarship.notes: Award is recorded under its exact official title, 'International Student Merit Scholarship', as published by Charles Sturt University; the assigned row carried the generic family label 'Charles Sturt University International Scholarships'. This is one award inside CSU's wider international scholarship family, which on the awarding body's own site also includes the Vice-Chancellor International Excellence Scholarship (50% tuition fee reduction), the International Student Success Scholarship (15% from the second session), the International Student Success Merit Scholarship (30% from the second session), the International Diversity Merit Scholarship (30%), the International Diversity Scholarship (15%) and the International Student Support Scholarship (10%). funding_amount and funding_currency are null because the university publishes the benefit only as a percentage of tuition and publishes no fixed dollar figure for this award; the percentage is recorded verbatim in funding_label, benefits and coverage. The page states 'Closes: 11:59pm 31 Dec 2026' in the header but 'Applications are open until further advice' in the How to Apply section; the header date is recorded as deadline_date and the discrepancy is noted. No timezone is published for the 11:59pm cut-off, so deadline_central_timezone is null. No English language requirement is published on the award page, so english_requirement is null. No bond, service obligation or repayment obligation is published for this award, but the recipient accepts promotional and media obligations and the award can be suspended or terminated. Logo is null: every candidate logo URL on CSU's own domains returned HTTP 403 with text/html (a WAF block, not image bytes), which rule 7 of the logo contract excludes; details are in research_notes.logo. The international scholarship index page listed in catalogue_url was seen in the breadcrumb of the fetched award page but was not itself fetched, so it is not in source_citations.

programme_detail_official.description: The International Student Merit Scholarship is a Charles Sturt University tuition-fee reduction for new commencing international students, valued at a 25% fee discount for the entire duration of the course and deducted from tuition fees at the commencement of each session. It is awarded automatically by the admissions team when an applicant applies for an approved course in internal/on-campus mode at an eligible campus, with no separate application process, and the outcome is advised with the offer letter. Academic entry is assessed either through an Australian AQF Level 7 progression route or through published Year 12 equivalent thresholds of 75 per cent for most undergraduate degrees and 85 per cent for Allied Health courses other than Nursing. There is no bond, no living-cost component and no travel component.
programme_detail_official.coverage: Covers a 25% reduction in tuition fees for the entire duration of the course, deducted from tuition fees at the commencement of each session. Does not cover the remaining 75% of tuition, accommodation, living costs, travel, visa or the e-COE, and no bond attaches to the award.

application_readiness_checklist: Pick your course from CSU's published list of approved courses and check the entry-score threshold attached to it before you apply: 75 per cent Year 12 equivalent for most undergraduate degrees, 85 per cent for Allied Health except Nursing.

Apply to an approved course in internal/on-campus mode at Albury-Wodonga, Bathurst, Dubbo, Melbourne, Orange, Port Macquarie, Sydney or Wagga Wagga. Do not rely on an online-mode offer, which is expressly ineligible.
No separate scholarship form exists. Your CSU admission application is the scholarship application, so do not spend time hunting for a scholarship portal.

If you are relying on the Australian academic progression route, have your AQF Level 7 or above completion certificate and date ready, and make sure the completion date is within 12 months of your course commencement date.
Keep the offer letter, because the scholarship decision travels with it, and pay the fee deposit promptly so the e-COE is issued.
Budget for the remaining 75% of tuition plus accommodation, living costs, travel and visa yourself: this award is a fee discount, not a funded place.
Read the promotional conditions before you accept: you will be expected to join the student body, give testimonials, be photographed, and sign a media release.
Do not accept another Charles Sturt-funded tuition fee scholarship alongside this one, and do not assume it can be combined with a CSU-funded award.
common_rejection_risks: Applying for an online-mode course, which is expressly excluded from the scholarship even though CSU offers online degrees.
Applying through a CSU international partner rather than to a CSU campus, which is also excluded.
Missing the academic entry threshold for the specific approved course, where Allied Health and most other undergraduate degrees carry different thresholds.

Being a continuing student, or transferring from another CSU course or applying with advanced standing without confirming eligibility first; the page excludes transferring students while noting that some advanced-standing cases are still treated as commencing.
Holding an Australia Awards or Research Training Program scholarship, which disqualifies the applicant from this award.
Submitting through an exchange or study abroad channel rather than a degree admission.
Accepting a second CSU-funded tuition fee scholarship, which terminates eligibility for this one.
Missing the 11:59pm 31 Dec 2026 cut-off, since assessment runs through the admissions process and late offers may fall outside the published window.
estimated_uncovered_costs: The remaining 75% of tuition fees for every session of the course; the award is a partial remission only.
All accommodation costs, whether on campus or private.
All living costs: food, local transport, utilities, phone and internet.
Overseas student visa charges, medical screening and insurance.
Air travel to and from Australia, and any pre-arrival costs.
The Confirmation of Enrolment fee deposit and other student levies not covered by the reduction.
Books, course materials, software and equipment.
Any English language testing cost, if you need a test score for admission; the award page publishes no English requirement, so nothing is reimbursed.
document_audit: There is no separate scholarship document list. Your evidence package is your admission application to an approved on-campus course.
Academic transcript or certificate showing the Year 12 equivalent score, assessed against the threshold for your specific approved course.
AQF Level 7 or above qualification and completion date, if using the Australian academic progression route.
Offer letter, which is the document that carries the scholarship decision.
Fee deposit receipt and e-COE confirmation.
Signed media release, which the University will ask for after award.

research_notes.logo: logo_override is null and this is an honest null, not a failure to look. Charles Sturt University serves its marks from its own first-party asset host, and every candidate URL was probed live on 2026-10-03. Probed and rejected: https://cdn.csu.edu.au/__data/assets/file/0009/2823219/CSU_Logo_01.svg (the header logo referenced in the fetched award page markup) returned HTTP 403 with content-type text/html and 5567 bytes; https://cdn.csu.edu.au/__data/assets/file/0010/3192175/CSU-logo-crest-footer.svg returned HTTP 403 text/html 5618 bytes; https://cdn.csu.edu.au/__data/assets/file/0011/3192176/CSU-logo-stacked-footer.svg returned HTTP 403 text/html 5624 bytes; https://www.csu.edu.au/__data/assets/file/0009/2823219/CSU_Logo_01.svg returned HTTP 403 text/html 5567 bytes; https://www.csu.edu.au/favicon.ico returned HTTP 403 text/html 5416 bytes; https://www.csu.edu.au/apple-touch-icon.png returned HTTP 403 text/html 5465 bytes. Every response is an HTML WAF interstitial rather than image bytes, which rule 7 of the logo contract excludes outright, and a 403 body is exactly the 'unprobed or HTML' failure the contract tells us not to ship. No aggregator, CDN mirror, Wikimedia, stock site or social asset was used as a fallback, and no plausible-looking URL was invented. logo_host_taken is false for the substituted row, so an override would have been a legitimate new entry had any URL returned image bytes. Recommend a re-probe from a network that is not blocked by CSU's WAF before merging a logo for csu.edu.au.

research_notes.substitution: Substituted the assigned slot b133 row 'Universiti Malaya International Undergraduate Scholarships' (host um.edu.my, Malaysia) for Charles Sturt University's International Student Merit Scholarship, the assigned slot b124 row 'Charles Sturt University International Scholarships' (host csu.edu.au, Australia, bachelor eligible, logo_host_taken false, unclaimed by any other agent in research/bachelor at the time of writing). Reason for substituting: on the awarding body's own reachable official pages, Universiti Malaya publishes no bachelor's-level scholarship or waiver open to international students, only an admissions fee schedule and application charges, so no scholarship could be recorded without inventing one. Evidence gathered on um.edu.my domains on 2026-10-03 before substituting: (1) https://www.um.edu.my/scholarships-and-financial-assistancers states the Scholarships and Loans Unit exists to 'provide information on financial sponsorship to the local undergraduate students and financial aid schemes to the postgraduate students', i.e. its remit is local undergraduate plus postgraduate, and the site's own navigation sends 'Scholarship & Financial Aid / Undergraduate' to https://aasd.um.edu.my/financial-aid-for-undergraduate; (2) that aasd.um.edu.my page is unreachable from this environment on every attempt - DNS resolves to 103.18.3.114 and TCP port 443 connects, but the server returns an empty response with no TLS or HTTP payload, giving curl HTTP 000 and Playwright ERR_EMPTY_RESPONSE on https, http, IPv4-forced, TLS-1.2-pinned and alternate-hostname attempts, and the same empty response affects bendahari.um.edu.my, hep.um.edu.my and umsitsguide.um.edu.my while www.um.edu.my, study.um.edu.my and apply.um.edu.my respond normally, so the block is server-side rather than a DNS failure; (3) https://study.um.edu.my/faqs-amp-info, the official prospective-student FAQ page, contains the heading 'Fee Waiver' with the statement 'We regret to inform you that no fee waiver are available for application or admission fees', and contains no scholarship or waiver provision for international undergraduates; (4) the official UM International Booklet PDF at https://study.um.edu.my/doc/booklets/International%20Booklet%20-%20Updated%2015%20Dec%202025.pdf was downloaded and text-extracted in full (32 pages, 30949 characters of extractable text) and searched for scholarship, waiver, bursary, bond, discount and waive: zero matches. Its contents cover 'Our Programmes and Tuition Fees', i.e. a fee schedule, not a scholarship. The only international undergraduate scholarship located on an official um.edu.my page is the PTE x Universiti Malaya Scholarship 2026, which was already recorded by another agent in this batch in research/bachelor/57-pte-universiti-malaya-scholarship.json, so recording it again here would have created a duplicate. Australia is an allowed region and csu.edu.au has no entry in EXISTING_AWARDS.json, and row b124 is unclaimed, so this substitution adds a genuinely new, verified, bachelor's-level international award. The Charles Sturt University award was verified directly on csu.edu.au, the awarding body's own domain, and is a real tuition-fee remission rather than a fee table.
research_notes.degree_level_confirmed: Confirmed on the awarding body's own award page, which lists Bachelor's degrees in the published table of approved courses with their entry-score requirements (for example Bachelor of Accounting, Bachelor of Engineering (Honours), Bachelor of Information Technology (with specialisations), Bachelor of Nursing), each carrying the published threshold 'Scores above 75% in Year 12 (or equivalent study)' and Allied Health degrees at 85 per cent. The award page states the reduction applies 'throughout the entire duration of the course' and is deducted from tuition fees at the commencement of each session, i.e. across the whole degree, so degree_levels is set to Bachelor's and the same page also covers eligible postgraduate degrees, which is recorded in degree_levels rather than generalised.
